ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, point A is an arbitrary point on the graph of the inverse proportion function $y= \frac{2}{x}$ ($x>0$). Line segment $AB$ is parallel to the $x$-axis and intersects the graph of the inverse proportion function $y= -\frac{3}{x}$ at point B. A square $\square ABCD$ is formed with $AB$ as a side, where points $C$ and $D$ lie on the $x$-axis. What is the area $S_{\square ABCD}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw $AF \perp x$-axis at point $F$ and $BE \perp x$-axis at point $E$ from points $A$ and $B$, respectively.

Since $\square ABCD$, 

it follows that $AB \parallel x$-axis,

hence quadrilateral $ABEF$ is a rectangle,

thus $S_{\square ABCD} = S_{\text{rectangle } ABEF}$,

since $A$ and $B$ are located on the graphs of inverse proportion functions $y=\frac{2}{x}$ and $y=-\frac{3}{x}$, respectively,

it follows that $S_{\text{rectangle } ABEF} = 2 + 3 = 5$,

therefore, $S_{\square ABCD} = \boxed{5}$.

method.method_draft: Use coordinates with the top height as a parameter. From the image, note that A is on the right branch labeled y=2/x, B is on the left branch labeled y=-3/x, AB is horizontal, and C,D lie on the x-axis as the lower side of the square. From the text, AB is parallel to the x-axis and ABCD is a square. Let the common y-coordinate of A and B be h>0. Then A=(2/h,h) and B=(-3/h,h). Hence AB=2/h-(-3/h)=5/h. Since the square has AB as a side and its opposite side lies on the x-axis, the side length also equals the vertical distance h. Therefore h=5/h, so h^2=5. The square area is h^2=5.
